description: Enable window movement, opening and closing effects. When false, none of these effects run.

Choose the material for movement, opening and closing. Liquid deforms the edges; paper crumples into a ball and moves without deformation; cloth drapes and flutters; swarm breaks the window into creature-shaped pieces; bubble inflates a soap film, sloshes while moving and bursts on close. Invalid names are rejected.
Swarm sprite name in the sprites directory, with or without .png, or an explicit PNG path. The sheet has four columns and two rows of frames; transparency defines the silhouette.
Number of swarm creatures per window. Each carries a piece of the window, so fewer creatures mean larger pieces.
Swarm creature travel speed in logical pixels per second.
Time in seconds over which swarm creatures arrive or leave in random order when a window opens or closes. Movement releases them over half this time. Zero makes them arrive or leave together.
How strongly nearby swarm creatures travel together. Zero lets each find its own way.
How much swarm creatures avoid and bump off each other while travelling. Zero lets them pass through each other.
Swarm acceleration and grip. Higher values hold formation during faster movement and turn more sharply; lower values break apart sooner and trail farther.
How quickly swarm creatures regroup and merge back into the window. Lower values make them mill about longer.
How much swarm creatures wander and hesitate while travelling. Zero makes them follow their routes steadily.
Variation in each swarm creature's speed, grip and route curvature. Zero makes them travel straight and alike.
Deform windows while they move. This does not affect opening or closing effects.
Let workspace slides trigger movement effects. When false, ordinary movement, opening and closing are unaffected.
Liquid movement deformation strength. Zero moves windows without deformation.
Liquid resistance to flow during movement. Higher values make it thicker and more cohesive.
Liquid stiffness and recovery speed during movement. Higher values snap back faster.
Liquid inertia after movement stops. Zero settles without overshoot.
Random variation between windows and movements. Zero makes liquid movement identical.
Cloth movement deformation strength. Zero moves windows without deformation.
Horizontal springiness of the curtain's top edge during movement. Zero keeps it stiff; higher values allow more gathering and rebound. The lower curtain remains free-flowing.
Cloth movement gravity multiplier. One is normal gravity; zero disables gravity. Lower values let fabric lift more easily. Opening and closing are unaffected.
Cloth movement ripple strength. Zero removes varying gusts, but movement still bends the sheet.
Light and shadow on cloth movement folds. Zero draws them unlit.
Highlight strength on cloth movement folds. Zero removes highlights.
Variation in cloth movement between windows. Zero gives every window the same motion.
How much the trailing bubble film lags, ripples and overshoots during movement. Zero moves windows without deformation.
Rate at which small bubbles form on stretched film, slide to the trailing edge and detach. Zero forms none.
Amount of thin soap film a fast-moving window leaves behind before it drains and breaks up. Zero leaves none.

Shape surface tension pulls a moving bubble toward. Pillow rounds the corners and gently bulges the sides; ellipse keeps the window's proportions; circle makes a disc regardless of its proportions. Invalid names are rejected.
How far a window moving at shape_speed contracts toward its bubble shape before returning to a rectangle when stopped. Zero keeps it rectangular.
Window speed in logical pixels per second at which bubble shape contraction reaches its full amount. Slower windows contract proportionally less.
Animate windows as they open using the selected style. When false, windows open without this effect; movement is unaffected.
Liquid pop-out size and deformation strength when opening. Zero removes the pop-out.
Colour of the liquid at the opening edge, in ARGB. Zero alpha draws no liquid.
Preferred opening edge for the first window on a workspace. Later windows use their placement. Invalid edges fall back to a valid edge.
Choose monitor edges (screen) or edges inside reserved areas (work_area) for the liquid pop-out.
Share of liquid pop-out travel applied as drag to the movement field. Zero makes the pop rigid.
Liquid pop-out stiffness and recovery speed. Higher values snap back faster.
Liquid pop-out inertia. Zero settles without overshoot.
Time in seconds for the paper ball to uncrumple into the window.
Paper crumple tightness when opening. Higher values make a smaller, more creased ball.
Light and shadow on paper creases when opening. Zero draws the folds unlit.
Random choice and mirroring of the opening paper crumple for each window. Zero uses the same crumple for every window.
Time in seconds for the gathered curtain to spread from its top edge and settle flat.
Opening origin for the first cloth window on a workspace, used when the closing side is origin. Later windows use their placement. Cloth still opens in place.
Choose monitor edges (screen) or edges inside reserved areas (work_area) for the cloth opening origin.
Cloth gust strength when opening. Zero removes flutter, but gravity still moves the sheet.
Light and shadow on cloth folds when opening. Zero draws them unlit.
Highlight strength on cloth folds when opening. Zero removes highlights.
Variation in cloth opening motion between windows. Zero gives every window the same motion.
Screen sides swarm creatures enter from for the first window on a workspace. Later windows use the side where they appear (see Edge choice).
Time in seconds for bubble inflation, outer film rupture, flattening, splat and elastic settling.
Animate windows as they close using the selected style. When false, windows close natively; movement is unaffected.
Liquid drain deformation strength when closing. Zero closes the window natively.
Colour of the liquid at the closing edge, in ARGB. Zero alpha draws no liquid.
Preferred closing edge for the last window on a workspace when side is auto. Other windows use their placement. Invalid edges fall back to a valid edge.
Liquid exit edge: the side of appearance (auto), nearest valid edge, opening origin, or a fixed edge. Invalid preferred edges fall back to the normal edge selection.
Choose monitor edges (screen) or edges inside reserved areas (work_area) for the liquid exit.
Show a small edge-liquid splash where a window closes. When false, it closes without liquid.
Liquid drain stiffness and recovery speed. Higher values snap back faster.
Liquid closing dive acceleration. Higher values make the dive advance faster.
Time in seconds for the window to crumple into a paper ball and vanish.
Paper crumple tightness when closing. Higher values make a smaller, more creased ball.
Light and shadow on paper creases when closing. Zero draws the folds unlit.
Random choice and mirroring of the closing paper crumple for each window. Zero uses the same crumple for every window.
Time in seconds for the top rod to carry the curtain beyond the selected screen edge.
Preferred cloth closing edge for the last window on a workspace when side is auto. Invalid edges fall back to a valid edge.
Cloth exit edge: the side of appearance (auto), nearest valid edge, opening origin, or a fixed edge. Invalid preferred edges fall back to the normal edge selection.
Choose monitor edges (screen) or edges inside reserved areas (work_area) for cloth edge selection. Cloth travels beyond the actual screen before disappearing.
Cloth gust strength when closing. Zero removes flutter, but gravity still moves the sheet.
Light and shadow on cloth folds when closing. Zero draws them unlit.
Highlight strength on cloth folds when closing. Zero removes highlights.
Variation in cloth closing motion between windows. Zero gives every window the same motion.
Screen sides swarm creatures leave through for the last window on a workspace. Otherwise they use the side where the window sits (see Edge choice).
Time in seconds for the bubble film to thin, tear, retract into strands and droplets, and for the droplets to evaporate.
